title: Tenant-scoped compliance delivery and formatting pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Customers running Redwood Private and Dedicated ask for tenant-scoped, auditable compliance exports that can be scheduled, delivered to customer-owned endpoints, and keep strict residency and retention guarantees. Current exports are ad-hoc and lack standardized PDF rendering, canonical CSV schemas, delivery telemetry, and tenant-aware routing.

This ticket defines a product-level pipeline to produce scheduled compliance reports (PDF and CSV), surface them in a compliance dashboard, and deliver them via configurable transports (S3/HTTPS/SFTP/email) while respecting data residency and retention policies per tenant. The pipeline must generate verifiable artifacts (signed manifests, checksums), emit detailed delivery telemetry, and allow admins to configure frequency, timezone, and residence-targeting rules.
acceptance_criteria: Admins can create a scheduled export for a tenant with: format=(pdf|csv), frequency=(daily|weekly|monthly|custom cron), timezone, retention-apply-policy, and target transport with credentials.

Generated PDF must include a standardized header with tenant id, residency region, export time (UTC), applied retention snapshot, and cryptographic checksum manifest attached as a separate file in the artifact bundle.
CSV exports follow documented canonical schema with a version identifier and include metadata row(s) describing field provenance and applied redaction rules.

Delivery supports tenant-owned S3 (AWS/GCP), HTTPS webhook with HMAC signature, and SFTP endpoints. Retries/backoff and non-delivery alerts must be implemented; failed deliveries surface in console and emit an incident metric.

Export generation respects tenant data residency: exports for EU-residency tenants are produced in eu-region infra and never leave approved regions in transit (use region-to-region encryption/transfer methods documented).
Retention enforcement shown in manifest: records excluded due to retention policy must be annotated in the manifest with counts and filter criteria.
Compliance dashboard shows scheduled jobs, last run status, artifact URLs, delivery history with timestamps, and per-tenant SLA attainment (delivery success rate, mean time-to-deliver).
Operations: runtime cost estimate for daily/weekly jobs and an autoscaling plan for spike generation (backfill), validated with load test generating 1,000 concurrent tenant exports.
notes: Avoid duplicating existing 'evidence export' flows — this pipeline focuses on tenant-scoped scheduling, signed artifacts, and standardized formatting for downstream ingestion by auditors.
PDF renderer must support page-level redaction markers; use HTML-to-PDF pipeline with templating that can be audited (template versioning).
CSV schema should be versioned and discoverable via /compliance/schema/{version} endpoint for ingestion by customer tools.

For Private deployments where external delivery is restricted, provide an 'on-prem pull' option (signed presigned URLs valid for a short window) and an operator-run offload command documented in the admin guide.
Consider adding a deliverability test job per tenant to validate credentials and network path before first scheduled run.
implementation_plan: Produce a small API surface: POST /api/v1/tenants/{tid}/exports to create job (payload validates format, frequency, target).
Backend worker: queue-based generator with tenant routing that picks infra region based on tenant residency metadata.
Renderer: HTML templating service + wkhtmltopdf or headless-chrome with strict CSP; CSV serializer with streaming to avoid OOMs for large datasets.
Delivery module: pluggable transports (S3, HTTPS, SFTP, email). Implement credential vault integration (KMS) and ephemeral credential usage for S3/GCS targets.
Dashboard: add scheduled-jobs view to Console with job timeline, last run, size, and delivery latency histograms.
Observability: emit metrics (export_generation_time_ms, delivery_success, delivery_failures, bytes_generated) and structured logs that include tenant_id, job_id, residency_region.
Security: manifest signing using customer-scoped key or server key with verifiable signature; include manifest checksum in header and as separate .sha256 file for each bundle.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Internal beta): Enable for compliance and solutions teams on Hosted and Dedicated for 5 pilot tenants. Monitor generation success and delivery failures for two weeks.
Phase 2 (Customer opt-in): Allow select customers to enable pipeline; collect feedback on PDF format and CSV schema. Enable SFTP delivery for Private customers via operator onboarding.

Phase 3 (General availability): Turn on UI discoverability, default retention snapshots, and automation for retries; publish admin docs and run migration script for any existing ad-hoc exports to the scheduled model.
Rollouts will include canary percentage gating by tenant count (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and an automatic rollback if delivery_success < 98% over a 24h window.
metrics: Mean time to generate (seconds) and mean time to deliver (minutes)
Number of exports generated per hour and total bytes produced
Percentage of exports produced in-correct-region (compliance check)
Number of manifest verification failures reported by customers
risks: Large exports may cause generator memory pressure; need streaming and chunking path to mitigate.
Cross-region transfers for customers with mixed residence may introduce regulatory complexity — require legal sign-off for each transfer mode.
Delivery credential misconfiguration could cause repeated failures — provide pre-send validation and simulated delivery test.
PDF renderer differences between headless browsers could cause layout drift; maintain snapshot tests for templates.
updates: 2025-02-20: Scoped CSV schema fields; ENG to draft serializer and schema registry entry.
2025-02-25: Security reviewed initial signing options; choose KMS-backed signing for hosted and customer-key option for Dedicated/Private.
2025-03-01: UX mockups reviewed; minor changes to timezone selector (support tenant-level default).
2025-03-04: Engineering spike scheduled to validate pdf renderer performance under 200 concurrent jobs.
